notes: Summary: Elmbridge (industrial robotics + remote ops) evaluating Dedicated capacity + Private control plane for low-latency control-loop inference.
Primary ask: throughput guarantee for 2000 TPS embeddings peak and 300 concurrent low-latency chat sessions (95th pct latency < 120ms).
SLA focus: targeted uptime 99.95% for regional capacity + defined credit schedule; legal asked for options to escalate to 99.99 if costed separately.

Credit schedule proposed by Redwood (initial): 99.95-100% = no credit; 99.80-99.95% = 10% monthly credit; 99.50-99.80% = 25% credit; <99.50% = 50% credit. Elmbridge requested carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

Maintenance windows: Redwood proposed quarterly maintenance 4 hours per month (or aggregated quarterly), 72-hr advance notice. Elmbridge requests no maintenance during their regional business hours (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 local) and <30-min rolling restarts for model hotfixes.

Support SLA: P1 (system down / severe degradation) 15-min acknowledgement, 1-hr initial response, 4-hr remediation target; P2 (severe perf regressions) 1-hr ack, 8-hr remediation target. Elmbridge insists on dedicated escalation contact during ramp/launch for first 90 days.

Routing/fallback requirement: Redwood to provide automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant (latency SLO relaxed) before dropping requests; Elmbridge wants explicit throttling vs silent failures.

Quant / reserved GPU planning: Elmbridge requires upfront planning for reserved 8xA100-equivalent GPUs per region with autoscale buffer of +30% during predicted peak windows. Want a quarterly capacity review and 60-day scale-up notice.

POC results: load test 2026-02-20 (ff_20260220_loadtest) showed steady-state embeddings throughput 1.8k TPS with 95th pct token latency 95ms using continuous batching; burst spikes hit 2.5k TPS with 95th pct 170ms (need routing tweaks).
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable tail latency — occasional spikes break our control loops. Credits are helpful, but we need concrete preemptive fallbacks.'

Legal notes: Elmbridge legal wants specific blackout periods excluded from uptime calc, explicit definition of "availability" (control plane vs data plane), and granular credit flows (invoice credit vs cash refund).
Financial: Procurement team will consider extended term to 24 months in exchange for tighter SLO (cost uplift TBD).
